name: SiCamore Semi
old_description: More efficient drivetrains using semiconductor technologies based on Wide Band Gap (WBG) materials such as Silicon Carbide (SiC) are enabling engineers to achieve high voltage (1.2 – 3.3KV) and high power demands in a cost-effective way.
about:
SiCamore Semi operates a pure-play semiconductor foundry in Bend, Oregon. The company describes itself as a U.S.-based boutique foundry with three decades of experience in wafer fabrication, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly provided.

The foundry specializes in high-power, high-voltage wide-bandgap devices using silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) on 100 mm and 150 mm wafers. Its process flow covers photolithography with ASML 5000 I-line steppers and Karl Suss aligners, thin-film deposition (sputtering, PVD, CVD, PECVD, e-beam evaporation), frontside and backside metallization, thermal oxidation and diffusion, wet and dry etching (RIE), rapid thermal annealing, and ion implantation (cold and hot). SiC-specific steps include high-temperature implant and anneal, gate oxidation with nitric oxide anneal, and a dedicated gold wafer fab for high-reliability, radiation-hardened, and RF devices. Additional partner services encompass device design, wafer thinning, dicing, packaging, and test.

SiCamore serves electric-vehicle, medical, industrial, aerospace and defense, and academic customers. It supplies SiC diodes, MOSFETs, JBSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs, and Si SGTOs/SDIODEs for industrial power and switching applications. The company also collaborates with universities on NASA, NSF, DOE, and DOD grants focused on space, grid, weapons, EV, data-center, and communications technologies, and it targets U.S. military, intelligence, and government agencies alongside commercial transportation, telecommunications, and healthcare infrastructure markets.

The company states its mission is to deliver innovative power-semiconductor solutions through the development of silicon and wide-bandgap technologies. It aims to become the leading power-semiconductor facility in the U.S. Northwest for advanced wide-bandgap device fabrication, integration, and testing, emphasizing a stable, ITAR-certified environment for aerospace and defense programs.
